takeaway: Adrenal arteries: superior from inferior phrenic, middle from abdominal aorta, inferior from renal artery. One adrenal vein per gland: left to left renal vein, right to IVC.

answer.text: The middle adrenal artery is derived from the abdominal aorta.
answer.say: The middle adrenal artery is derived from the abdominal aorta.

lines.text: The adrenal gland, the yellow cap on the kidney, is usually supplied by three arteries: superior, middle and inferior.
The middle adrenal artery comes straight from the abdominal aorta. That is the correct statement.
The superior artery comes from the inferior phrenic artery, not from the renal artery.
And the inferior adrenal artery comes from the renal artery, not from the inferior phrenic.
The gland drains by one adrenal vein, not three. On the left it joins the left renal vein, on the right the inferior vena cava.
So the middle adrenal artery from the abdominal aorta is the right answer.
